prompt:
Use case: identity-preserve. Asset type: one transparent production sprite sheet for an original desktop pet.
Image 1 is the identity and costume reference (original blue-haired chibi girl holding a book). Image 2 is a supporting reference for a comical distressed expression. Edit into an ANIME COMEDY "PICKED UP AND PANICKING IN MID-AIR" eight-frame animation, not dancing, not waving hello.
Exactly FOUR columns and TWO rows, eight equal cells, read left to right top to bottom, canvas aspect 4:3 (target 1448x1086). Each cell has portrait aspect 2:3. IMPORTANT: character must occupy ONLY the central 58% of cell width and 72% of cell height. Leave at least 18% entirely transparent space on both LEFT and RIGHT of EVERY cell, 12% above hair and 12% below shoes. All limbs, hair and symbols stay well inside their own cell. No overlapping neighboring characters. All eight cells have the same scale and anchor. Transparent empty gutters, no grid lines, no labels, numbers or text. True transparent alpha background, no gradient, glow, checkerboard or shadows.

Keep original identity, chibi face, blue/cyan wavy long hair, whale hair ornament, cream cardigan, navy dress, ribbons, white socks and navy shoes. Keep the skirt fully covering the body, camera at eye level and both shoes clearly visible. Remove the book during this action. Front-facing upper torso hangs upright as if lifted by the back of the cardigan; shoulders are hunched in surprise. Hair hangs downward with small delayed follow-through. Expression uses recognizable anime comedy panic: squeezed > < eyes, a small wobbling open wail mouth and one small sweat bead TOUCHING the temple. Distressed and cute, no smile. Do not draw a hand holding her or an external person. Do not add floating text, exclamation marks, speed lines or large detached symbols.

Make a coherent eight-frame LOOP with clear in-betweens, not eight alternate static illustrations. Head and chest remain anchored and nearly unchanged in size. Both elbows are bent near the torso; forearms flutter in small frantic circular arcs, as someone awkwardly flaps to regain balance. Legs pedal in alternating bends in mid-air, rather than posing with one leg always extended. Frame 1: left knee bent up, right leg lower, left forearm a little higher; 2: lowering that knee and passing hands inward; 3: both knees halfway bent, hands pass neutral; 4: right knee rises and the forearms change direction; 5: right knee up, left leg lower, opposite forearm higher; 6: right knee lowers, hands travel back; 7: legs pass through neutral again; 8: smoothly approach frame 1. Adjacent poses change incrementally. Small torso rocking at most 3 degrees, no teleporting, spins or changing head proportions. Clean readable silhouette. No duplicate limbs, blur or ghost poses. Both arms and both legs anatomically coherent in every frame.
